title: LC-MT368-CrossProjectDependenciesAndReadiness
clause: Implement explicit, authorized cross-project dependencies and readiness without merging project authorities.

scope.summary: GOAL: Add typed dependency relations between project-qualified projects, WPs and MTs across the managed-project forest. Same-project dependencies follow normal project authority. Cross-project dependencies require explicit authorization over both endpoints, record who approved the edge and expose only privacy-safe blocker information. Readiness is derived from canonical dependency terminal states and gates. Edges reject cycles across project boundaries. Removing, archiving or reparenting a project cannot silently erase or retarget an external dependency.
forbidden_paths: Implicit cross-project dependencies inferred from links, parentage or paths
Dependency targets identified by bare WP/MT labels
Leaking denied blocker titles, paths or project existence
acceptance_criteria: Dependencies use project-qualified endpoints and support project, WP and MT targets without ambiguous bare-id resolution.
Creating or removing a cross-project edge requires explicit authorization over both endpoint scopes and stores an attributable approval receipt atomically through MT-367.
Cycle detection spans the canonical visible graph and fails closed when authorization prevents proving safety; no cross-project cycle can be committed.
Readiness and blocked queries return accurate typed reasons while replacing denied remote detail with a non-enumerating authorized blocker token.
Archive, reparent and deletion operations surface affected external edges for resolution and never silently remove or retarget them.
proof_targets: Multi-project dependency CRUD tests in real SurrealDB
Cross-project cycle and insufficient-visibility fail-closed tests
Mixed-authority privacy tests for blocker responses
Archive/reparent dependency-impact tests with atomic receipts

enforcement_boundaries: Both dependency endpoints are authorized independently.
Graph traversal cannot widen scope through an authorized local edge.
same_project_private_resource_cases: A local project member without the target private AccessSpace cannot attach to or inspect that target.
cross_account_negative_cases: A dependency cannot cross accounts without explicit authority at both endpoints and cannot reveal a denied remote target.
derived_resource_non_widening_cases: Readiness, blocker and lifecycle-impact projections preserve endpoint visibility and use privacy-safe tokens for denied details.
revocation_and_context_switch_cases: Endpoint revocation or project-context switch invalidates dependency mutation authority and refreshes readiness visibility.
metadata_side_channel_cases: Denied remote targets are non-enumerating and leak no title, kind, status, owner, project name, count or timing detail.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.reason: Record edge mutation, endpoint scopes, authorization receipts, readiness revision and cycle verdict without denied metadata.
Expose dangling edges, cycles, stale readiness and unresolved lifecycle impacts.
Record DEFERRED-with-reason if cross-project blocker and cycle watchers are unavailable; never silently skip.

risk_if_missed: Cross-project automation can run on ambiguous or unauthorized dependencies, leak private project data or deadlock through hidden cycles.

risks: A local user attaches to a private remote MT.
A hidden edge completes a cycle.
Bare ids resolve to the wrong project.
Archive silently deletes an external blocker.
minimum_controls: Lifecycle impact receipts and explicit resolution.

research_provenance.source: Approved 2026-08-27 project/subproject/task/prototype use cases; MT-365/367 contracts; current Locus dependency gaps; official SurrealDB graph relation and permission documentation.
research_provenance.selected_approach: Explicit typed graph edges with dual-endpoint authorization, privacy-safe readiness and atomic receipts.
